newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-O'LEARY APPOINTED TO ASSIST GRAHAM AT LEEDS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-O'LEARY APPOINTED TO ASSIST GRAHAM AT LEEDS.

text.p: Former Arsenal defender and Ireland international David O'Leary has been appointed assistant to new Leeds United manager George Graham, the premier league club said on Tuesday.
Graham, dismissed by Arsenal and then banned for 12 months for accepting illegal payments over transfer deals, replaced Howard Wilkinson at Leeds on September 10.
The 51-year-old Scot said O'Leary was the perfect man to help him train the club's first team and take charge while he was away searching for new players.
Graham coached O'Leary for eight of the 20 years the 38-year-old Irishman spent at Arsenal.
"I know if I am away, hopefully looking at players, David can take over. He knows exactly what is expected of him. He will put my ideas across and say what I believe," Graham said.
"He will hopefully give me the backing and wonderful service I need."
O'Leary, who played 12 games for Leeds in 1993 following a free transfer from Arsenal, said: "I shall try to help George Graham get Leeds back up where they belong.
"But I've been told I must be crazy. I have had offers since I left the game, but I didn't think they were right for me."
